title: The useRef Hook
description: Learn how to access DOM elements and persist values across renders.

data.text: **useRef** serves two purposes: accessing DOM elements directly and storing mutable values that persist across renders without causing re-renders when changed.
Attach a ref to any JSX element with the `ref` attribute. After React mounts the component, `ref.current` points to the DOM node.

data.text: useRef values survive across renders but do not trigger re-renders when mutated. This is useful for storing previous values, IDs, or any mutable value you don't want in state.

data.title: Ref Object
data.text: useRef returns `{ current: initialValue }`. You can read and write `ref.current` at any time without triggering React updates.

data.title: What Developers Use useRef For
items: Focusing inputs, buttons, or other focusable elements.
Storing interval or timeout IDs for cleanup.
Tracking previous values without causing re-renders.

terms.definition: An object with a current property that persists across renders.

An element in the browser's Document Object Model.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Stopwatch
data.description: Create a stopwatch that starts, stops, and resets using useRef.
steps: Use useState for the displayed time.
Use useRef to store the interval ID so you can clear it on stop or unmount.
Add Start, Stop, and Reset buttons.
data.expectedOutcome: A working stopwatch that cleans up its interval correctly.

items.question: Can I read ref.current during render?
items.answer: Yes, but only for values that do not depend on the DOM layout. For measurements that need the painted DOM, use useLayoutEffect.

items.question: Why doesn't changing ref.current re-render the component?
items.answer: That is by design. Refs are for values that should not trigger UI updates. If you need a re-render, use state.

items.question: Can I useRef inside a conditional?
items.answer: No. Like all hooks, useRef must be called unconditionally at the top level.

items.question: What is the difference between useRef and createRef?
items.answer: createRef creates a new ref object on every render. useRef returns the same ref object across renders, making it suitable for persisting values.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useRef persists values across renders without triggering re-renders.
Attach refs to DOM elements with the ref attribute.
Use refs for focus, measurements, timers, and previous values.
Prefer useRef over createRef in functional components.
data.takeaway: useRef gives you escape hatches for DOM access and mutable values. Next, you will learn to pass refs through components with forwardRef.
